headline: Potato farmers block Dhaka-Rangpur highway over cold storage fee hike
summary: Farmers and traders dumped potatoes on the road in Rangpur to protest a sharp increase in storage costs, causing traffic jams for over an hour.
details: Potato farmers and traders in Rangpur blocked the Dhaka-Rangpur highway on Wednesday to protest a significant hike in cold storage fees. Protesters dumped potatoes on the road as a symbolic gesture, halting traffic for about an hour and leaving over a hundred vehicles stranded.

The Rangpur District Potato Farmers and Traders Association alleged that storage fees have jumped from 250-300 BDT per bag last year to as much as 450 BDT this season. This increase comes at a time when market prices for potatoes are already low, leading to severe financial losses for farmers.

According to the farmers, it costs 15-17 BDT to produce one kg of potato, while it currently sells for 13-14 BDT. With storage and bagging costs adding another 10 BDT, the total cost per kg exceeds 25 BDT, making the fee hike unsustainable.

Protesters also highlighted a lack of sufficient cold storage facilities in the Rangpur division, which produces about 35% of the country's total potato crop. This shortage often forces farmers to sell their produce at low prices immediately after harvest.

A delegation led by Anwar Sadat, convener of the Rangpur District Krishak Dal, spoke with the protesters and promised a meeting with the Deputy Commissioner on Thursday. The blockade was lifted after the protesters warned of stricter actions if their demands were not met.
Police confirmed that the blockade ended around 1 PM and traffic on the Dhaka-Rangpur highway has since returned to normal.

headline_marked: HC sets precedent for [[priority hearing of death references]] in repression cases
headline: HC sets precedent for priority hearing of death references in repression cases
summary: The High Court has ordered that death references in cases involving repression of women and children be given priority, while another trial for child rape was concluded in just 8 working days.
details: The High Court has established a new precedent by ordering the priority hearing of death references in cases related to the repression of women and children.
This move aims to ensure faster justice for victims of gender-based violence and child abuse, reducing the long delays often seen in the legal process.
In a separate development highlighting judicial efficiency, a court has successfully concluded a child rape trial in only 8 working days.
These developments signal a push toward more streamlined legal proceedings for the most severe crimes against women and children in Bangladesh.
The priority hearing mandate will likely accelerate the process for death penalty appeals and references to the High Court.
caption:
Justice for women and children just got a faster track. The High Court mandates priority hearings for death references.

The High Court has established a new precedent by ordering the priority hearing of death references in cases related to the repression of women and children.
